name: Arcturus BW-3 'Bonesaw'
description:
A stun baton measuring 55 centimeters in length, delivering a focused electrical discharge through a hardened contact head designed for direct application. Unlike probe-based stun weapons, the BW-3 requires physical contact, which Arcturus markets as a feature — the weapon is a melee tool for close-quarters control that combines blunt-force impact with electrical incapacitation. The discharge cycles at 20 pulses per second, creating a sustained shock effect that continues as long as the contact head remains pressed against the target.

The BW-3 is standard equipment in Arcturus-managed detention facilities and has a reputation for misuse that Arcturus has done nothing to address. The weapon's sustained-contact design means it can be applied to a restrained subject for any duration the operator chooses, and the 20-pulse-per-second cycle creates a specific kind of pain that subjects describe as having their nervous system rewritten in real time. Detention oversight reports have documented BW-3 application lasting minutes against restrained detainees — far beyond any tactical justification.
specifications:
length: 55cm
contact discharge: 40,000 volts, 20 pulses/second
power source: Rechargeable cell, 200 applications per charge
impact rating: Equivalent to aluminum baseball bat
weight: 0.8 kg
tactical_use: Close-quarters subject control in detention, crowd control, and security operations. The BW-3 combines the deterrent effect of a visible melee weapon with electrical incapacitation capability. Primarily used against unarmed or restrained subjects.
cultural_context: The BW-3 is the weapon most associated with institutional violence in GLMZ. Detention survivors describe it with the kind of specificity that indicates trauma — the exact sound it makes, the precise sensation, the way the pulses feel different depending on where the contact head is applied. 'Getting the bonesaw' is Shelf slang for any experience of systematic, methodical cruelty.
known_users: Known to be available on black market for Φ500
story_hooks: A former detention guard has come forward with BW-3 application logs showing that specific detainees were subjected to sustained electrical discharge on a schedule — not as punishment, but as what appears to be a systematic experiment in pain tolerance mapping.

Modified BW-3 units have appeared in the Shelf with the safety limiters removed, allowing discharge levels that cause cardiac arrest. They're being sold for Φ200, and someone is flooding the market deliberately.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist baton with an oversized contact head — chunky and deliberately intimidating. The design reads as purpose-built for pain rather than precision. Thick shaft tapers slightly toward a ribbed grip, then flares dramatically into a reinforced striking head roughly the size of a clenched fist, faceted for contact pressure distribution.
physical_description.dimensions: 55 cm overall length. Contact head approximately 8 cm wide × 6 cm deep. Grip section 12 cm. Shaft diameter 2.8 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced — 0.8 kg distributed toward the contact head. Feels purposeful in hand, designed to be swung with authority but controlled enough for one-handed application against restrained subjects.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer frame with carbon-composite core. Contact head is hardened steel with embedded electrical conductors. Internal architecture houses capacitor array and power regulation systems.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer body with a brushed-steel contact head showing faint oxidation marks and micro-scratches from repetitive contact applications. Power indicator strip along shaft finished in semi-gloss black.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with gunmetal steel contact head. Subtle blue accent lines running along the grip indicate active power state when charged.
physical_description.grip_texture: Deeply textured rubberized polymer with aggressive grip ridges. Designed to prevent slipping during sustained application. Slightly tacky to the touch, engineered for reliability in gloved hands.
distinctive_features: Oversized faceted contact head with visible electrical conductor ports
Power status indicator strip (blue when charged, amber when depleted) running 8 cm down the shaft
Circular reset port on grip base for battery cycling
Micro-serrations on contact head edges for pressure concentration
Two small venting ports near the grip where heat dissipates during operation
Slight discoloration marks on contact head from accumulated bioelectric residue
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS stamped in raised letters on the grip shaft. Serial plate (titanium) inset flush into polymer near the power port. Legal disclaimer etched in micro-text below manufacturer stamp.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn. Contact head shows surface scarring and faint burn marks from thousands of applications. Grip texture remains intact but polymer body exhibits minor scuffs and the patina of institutional use. Power indicator may be obscured by residue that requires periodic cleaning.
